mutant.description: THE CONTROL THAT HAD TO BE ABLE TO FAIL IS THE ALB DELIVERY ITSELF, and this face is built around it. The ALB grant carried NEITHER source condition before this change, so nothing established that logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com sends aws:SourceAccount. Adding a condition a service does not satisfy DENIES its writes -- and a refused S3 log delivery presents as an EMPTY PREFIX rather than an error, which is row Z-S49's silent-failure shape one bucket over. So the criterion grades this leg on a DELIVERED OBJECT after the apply and gives it no UNCOMPUTABLE branch. A pre-apply denominator was captured before the edit precisely so the after-read had something to be compared against.

The CloudFront leg also delivered twice more (79 -> 83, newest 21:18:26Z), so its permitted UNCOMPUTABLE branch was not needed. THE CONTROL ALSO PRODUCED A FINDING: because the ALB kept delivering through a condition it had never been tested against, logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com demonstrably DOES send aws:SourceAccount.

declared_exclusions.item: aws:SourceArn was added to NEITHER grant.
declared_exclusions.reason: The L4 floor says SourceArn ONLY where the service supports it, MEASURED per service and NEVER ASSUMED, because an asserted SourceArn is exactly how C-16 reached its wrong state. No instrument available to this seat establishes support for either principal -- egress to AWS documentation is prohibited, a census of all 34 bucket policies in the account found ZERO other grants to either principal, and no API reports which context keys a service sends. Not established, therefore not added. Row Z-S81 carries the instrument gap.

declared_exclusions.item: The ALB enablement oracle was NOT used to test a SourceArn condition.
declared_exclusions.reason: s3.tf:141-147 records that elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes performs a test write and fails loudly, so it COULD test such a condition -- but only by adding the condition first, and S29-AC2 makes a SourceArn added without a prior finding a FAIL even if the policy applies cleanly. Using the oracle to manufacture the finding that licenses the condition is the circularity the criterion exists to forbid.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S29-AC1 -- BOTH GRANTS CARRY SourceAccount, READ ON THE APPLIED PLANE: get-bucket-policy after, with both statements quoted in full, showing aws:SourceAccount present on each. The BEFORE state is quoted from this face (CloudFront: present; ALB: absent) as the comparison. Denominator: 2 of 2 grants.
acceptance.invocation: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket opal-data-security, before the edit and after the apply
acceptance.output_evidence: BEFORE, re-grounded by this seat at 20:57:05Z and matching the face's cut read exactly: 3 statements -- DenyInsecureTransport (no source conditions, correctly, being principal-independent); AllowCloudFrontAccessLogDelivery SourceAccount PRESENT, SourceArn ABSENT; AllowALBAccessLogDelivery BOTH ABSENT. AFTER, read immediately post-apply, both service statements quoted in full: AllowCloudFrontAccessLogDelivery -- Principal Service delivery.logs.amazonaws.com, Action s3:PutObject, Resource arn:aws:s3:::opal-data-security/waf-logs/cloudfront-access/*, Condition StringEquals { aws:SourceAccount 313476888478, s3:x-amz-acl bucket-owner-full-control }. AllowALBAccessLogDelivery -- Principal Service logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com, Action s3:PutObject, Resource arn:aws:s3:::opal-data-security/waf-logs/alb-opal-gateway/*, Condition StringEquals { aws:SourceAccount 313476888478, s3:x-amz-acl bucket-owner-full-control }. DENOMINATOR: 2 of 2 service grants carry aws:SourceAccount. Principals, actions and resources are UNCHANGED on both; the only delta in the whole document is the one added condition key.
acceptance.denominator: 3 policy statements read before and after; 2 of 2 service grants now carrying aws:SourceAccount; 1 condition key added in total.
acceptance.status_reason: The floor's non-negotiable half is met on both grants and read on the applied plane rather than inferred from the plan. The DenyInsecureTransport statement correctly carries no source condition -- it is principal-independent and a source condition there would be meaningless.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S29-AC2 -- THE SourceArn DECISION IS MEASURED PER SERVICE, NOT ASSERTED: for EACH principal, a stated finding on whether it sends a SourceArn for this delivery type, with the source of that finding cited, and the resulting condition present or deliberately absent. A SourceArn added without that finding is a FAIL even if the policy applies cleanly -- that is the exact method that produced the defect. A measured negative is a PASS.
acceptance.invocation: aws s3api list-buckets then get-bucket-policy across all 34 buckets in the account (estate-precedent census); aws logs describe-delivery-sources / describe-deliveries and aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers (delivery-identity reads)
acceptance.output_evidence: PER-PRINCIPAL FINDING, and for BOTH it is the same: NOT ESTABLISHED, therefore NOT ADDED. delivery.logs.amazonaws.com (CloudFront standard logging v2, delivering via the CloudWatch Logs delivery path -- delivery source opal-portal-cloudfront-access on arn:aws:cloudfront::313476888478:distribution/EVTSA9VEHNZVH): whether it sends aws:SourceArn is NOT ESTABLISHED. logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com (ALB arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:313476888478:loadbalancer/app/opal-gateway/89166a68f337e5a4): NOT ESTABLISHED. Neither condition was added. THE SOURCE OF THE FINDING, CITED AS THE CRITERION REQUIRES -- three instruments tried, all three unavailable, none assumed absent: (1) AWS DOCUMENTATION is barred, CLAUDE.md's Agent Autonomy section excluding all egress off Opal infrastructure and requiring Andrew's explicit per-use word for any external vendor call; (2) ESTATE PRECEDENT is empty -- list-buckets enumerated 34 buckets and every get-bucket-policy was read, finding exactly ONE bucket that names either principal, opal-data-security itself, the subject of this change; (3) NO LIVE API reports which request-context keys a service principal populates. WHAT IS MEASURED, AND IT IS ABOUT THE OTHER KEY: aws:SourceAccount is now PROVEN for BOTH principals, and by the criterion's own kind of evidence rather than by assertion. CloudFront was already delivering through a grant carrying that condition; and the ALB, whose grant had never carried either condition, KEPT DELIVERING after this change added it -- object at 21:20:12Z. A condition a service does not satisfy denies its writes, so continued delivery is a positive measurement of the key. *** A FOURTH INSTRUMENT WAS CHECKED AFTER THIS ROW WAS FIRST WRITTEN, on the operator's prompt that comp-iam has been substantially upgraded, and it fails for a STRUCTURAL reason rather than a missing feature. comp-iam simulate is an applied-plane simulate-principal-policy wrapper that enforces the Rule 22a traps by construction -- ONE resource ARN (a comma-list is refused), an auto-derived positive control, and --no-control marking a resulting DENY as UNPROVEN rather than rc=1. It takes a ROLE, an action and a resource, and its --context flag lets the caller SUPPLY condition keys. It does not report, and cannot report, which keys an AWS SERVICE populates in a request. Simulation answers what a policy would decide GIVEN a context; the question here is what context the service SENDS, which is upstream of any simulator. So the count of instruments tried is FOUR, not three, and the finding is unchanged.
acceptance.denominator: 2 principals, each with a stated finding; FOUR instruments attempted per principal (documentation, estate precedent, live API, upgraded comp-iam simulate); 34 bucket policies censused for estate precedent, 1 hit and it is the subject.
acceptance.status_reason: NOT A PASS, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ROW. The criterion says a MEASURED NEGATIVE is a PASS. What this seat has is NOT ESTABLISHED, which is a different claim: a measured negative asserts the service does not send the key, and nothing measured here supports that assertion. Filing not-established as measured-negative would be the same overreach in the opposite direction that produced C-16's defect -- and this face exists precisely to remedy an asserted condition. NOT A FAIL EITHER: the criterion's substantive requirement is that no SourceArn be added without a finding, and none was added. The conservative branch of the floor was taken. THE TELL WORTH NAMING, because it is why this needed a status rather than a sentence: THE CONSERVATIVE ACTION AND THE UNVERIFIABLE ONE ARE THE SAME ACTION. Adding only SourceAccount is both what a measured negative would license and what an inability to measure forces, so the record must state which of the two it is -- they look identical in the world and are not the same claim. Row Z-S81 @e4d6f01558 carries the instrument gap with two named shapes for whoever owns it, neither taken here: authorise a single narrow documentation read, which is an egress decision and Andrew's; or amend this criterion to permit the ALB enablement oracle as the finding, which turns the circularity into a ruled sequence.

ALB LEG -- PASS, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED: 127 -> 132 objects, with ONE strictly after the apply -- waf-logs/alb-opal-gateway/AWSLogs/313476888478/elasticloadbalancing/us-east-1/2026/09/03/313476888478_elasticloadbalancing_us-east-1_app.opal-gateway.89166a68f337e5a4_20260903T2120Z_54.161.142.181_35soq9es.log.gz, 458B, LastModified 2026-09-03T21:20:12Z. acceptance.status_reason: Both legs deliver and the risky one is proven. The ALB grant gained a condition that had never been tested against that principal, and if the service did not send aws:SourceAccount the condition would have denied its writes -- silently, as an empty prefix rather than an error, which is exactly row Z-S49's shape. It kept delivering within ten minutes of the apply, against a pre-apply cadence of roughly five minutes. THE CONTROL THEREFORE PRODUCED A FINDING AS WELL AS A PASS: continued delivery through a newly-added condition is a positive measurement that logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com sends aws:SourceAccount. That is the measured evidence S29-AC2 could not obtain for SourceArn, obtained here for the other key by the criterion's own control.
